Apple has released the seventh iOS 27 developer beta. iOS 27 beta 7 continues Apple's beta cycle this summer, with the public release expected in September. We will be updating our devices and sharing what we find.

Apple releases seventh iOS 27 developer beta for testing

The seventh developer beta is now available to download through the Settings app on eligible iPhones. If you're registered with the Apple Developer Program, go to Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates and choose the iOS 27 Developer Beta.

The developer beta released today is expected to become the fifth public beta of iOS 27. The final version will officially arrive next month.

As with other beta software, expect bugs, reduced battery life, app compatibility issues, and other rough edges.

iOS 27 focused entirely on Siri AI

iOS 27 is arguably one of Apple's most AI-focused iPhone updates to date. The most prominent change is Siri AI—a rebuilt intelligent assistant powered by next-generation Apple Intelligence and new Apple Foundation Models.

Siri AI brings richer conversation, personalised context, broader world knowledge, awareness of on-screen content, and deeper app actions across the system.

On iPhone, Siri AI also features a new visual experience tied to the Dynamic Island, plus a dedicated Siri app for reviewing conversation history across devices.

Visual Intelligence also joins Siri, including a new Siri mode inside the Camera app and related improvements to iPhone Camera Control.

Apple Intelligence expands across multiple apps as well. iOS 27 brings AI-powered improvements to Photos, Safari, Passwords, Mail, Messages, Phone, Shortcuts, Home, and more. As we previously broke down when looking at Apple's new Foundation Models, some features will run on-device, while others will be handled through Private Cloud Compute.

More iOS 27 features and changes

Beyond Siri and Apple Intelligence, iOS 27 includes several iPhone-specific changes. Apple has improved the Liquid Glass design introduced last year, including a new Liquid Glass transparency slider for adjusting the look of the system interface.

There are also performance improvements for app launching, Photos loading, launching the camera in Low Power Mode, AirDrop transfers, and switching between Wi-Fi and cellular.

Other iPhone changes include keyword and star ratings in Photos, customisable slideshow playback, smoother camera operations, consecutive sends in Messages, Dual Capture on FaceTime, custom EQ for AirPods, new recovery options, easier Apple Pay card switching, and AI-generated wallpaper creation.

We're currently installing iOS 27 beta 7 and will update with anything notable. In the meantime, you can check out Apple's keynote lineup for a recap of everything new in iOS 27.

Found any changes in this iOS 27 beta 7? Drop them in the comments below!
